## Research Themes

My research sits primarily in applied microeconomics, with a focus on labour markets, crime, policing, and urban change. Across these areas, I study how individuals, institutions, and neighbourhoods respond to shocks, incentives, and local economic change.

### Labour Markets, Shocks, and Adjustment

I examine how workers and local labour markets respond to disruption and institutional change, including mass layoffs, workplace unionisation, and the labour-market consequences of COVID-19.

### Crime, Policing, and Neighbourhoods

A large part of my recent research uses highly disaggregated spatial data to study the geography of crime, civilian responses to policing, and the incentives that shape criminal behaviour.

### Urban Change and Local Economies

I am interested in neighbourhood composition, housing markets, high street decline, and the broader social consequences of local economic change.

### Health, Education, and Human Capital

I also work on questions in health and education economics, including how education shapes health-related behaviour and how family and individual circumstances affect later labour-market outcomes.

## Current Projects

- *The death of the "High Street"? Main street closures, social disorder and urban change* (with [Diego Zambiasi][diego-zambiasi]), revised and resubmitted
- *Juvenile courts and recidivism* (with [Bahadir Dursun][bahadir-dursun] and [Diego Zambiasi][diego-zambiasi]), revise and resubmit
- *How New Housing Changes Neighbourhoods: Economic and Social Effects of Local Supply Expansions* (with Edward Lee), revise and resubmit
- *Football matches and policing: Evidence from London* (with [Andy Chung][andy-chung], [James Reade][james-reade], and [Gennaro Rossi][gennaro-rossi]), revise and resubmit
- *Temperature, crime and policing: Evidence from UK geocoded data*, under review
- *Regional employment effects from mass lay-offs across European regions* (with [Wessel Vermeulen][wessel-vermeulen]), under review
- *Local Crime Without Electoral Sanction: Neighbourhood Public Safety and Incumbent Support in England and Wales*, under review
- *Gangs of London: What Online Gang Territory Maps Reveal About Crime and Policing* (with [Diego Zambiasi][diego-zambiasi]), under review

## Selected Papers

- [Crime prevention through private actors: Evidence from a policy change at a large UK supermarket chain](https://doi.org/10.1111/obes.70020) (with Wednesday Croft). Forthcoming in *Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics*.
- [Racial Disparities in Civilian Response to Police Use of Force: Evidence from London](https://doi.org/10.1093/bjc/azae037). *British Journal of Criminology* (2025).
- [Expected Returns to Crime and Crime Location](https://doi.org/10.1257/app.20220585) (with [Arnaud Chevalier][arnaud-chevalier] and [Tanya Wilson][tanya-wilson]). *American Economic Journal: Applied Economics* (2024).
- [Austerity, welfare cuts and hate crime: Evidence from the UK's Age of Austerity](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jue.2022.103439) (with Kerry Bray and [John Wildman][john-wildman]). *Journal of Urban Economics* (2024).
- [Mass layoffs and voting behaviour: Evidence from the UK](https://doi.org/10.1111/bjir.12749) (with [Wessel Vermeulen][wessel-vermeulen]). *British Journal of Industrial Relations* (2023).
- [Worker adjustment to unexpected occupational risk: Evidence from COVID-19](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.euroecorev.2022.104325) (with [Barbara Eberth][barbara-eberth] and [John Wildman][john-wildman]). *European Economic Review* (2022).
- [Housing subsidies and property prices: Evidence from England](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.regsciurbeco.2018.06.002) (with Stephen McDonald). *Regional Science and Urban Economics* (2020).
- [The causal relationship between education, health and health related behaviour: Evidence from a natural experiment in England](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhealeco.2011.05.015). *Journal of Health Economics* (2011).
